extracted.intended_audience: general public, journalists, researchers and public-relations professionals interested in aviation incidents and corporate crisis response
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative material relevant to how an airline (or corporation) should respond publicly to a high-profile customer-incident crisis, including statements, compensations, policy changes, and interaction with authorities. Useful for drafting or assessing crisis press releases and corporate communications after similar incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: timely_response
rubrics_metrics.description: Respond rapidly to the incident; delays or slow responses worsen public perception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PR experts criticized United's handling for not moving quickly enough; Rupert Younger said Munoz "should have moved more quickly". United initially issued statements the day after, and later issued additional statements—speed of an early, appropriate statement is emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: genuine_apology_and_taking_responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Issue a sincere apology that accepts responsibility rather than minimizing the incident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Later Munoz apologized saying "No one should ever be mistreated this way." PR commentary noted his later apology was more effective than the initial response; experts recommended being "more genuinely apologetic."

rubrics_metrics.name: avoid_euphemistic_or_defensive_language
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use corporate euphemisms or language that appears to downplay harm (e.g., 're-accommodate').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Munoz's earlier use of the word "re-accommodating" was widely ridiculed and criticized. Use plain, direct language instead of sanitizing terms that suggest minimization.

rubrics_metrics.name: consistency_between_internal_and_external_messaging
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure internal communications align with public statements; contradictory internal messages damage credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Munoz sent an internal email commending crew actions while public statements later apologized—this inconsistency provoked backlash and calls for resignation.

rubrics_metrics.name: specific_remedial_actions_and_timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Announce concrete policy changes, corrective actions, and deadlines rather than vague promises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: United promised a report by April 30 and made immediate policy changes (e.g., not using police for involuntary bumping, booking crews earlier); PR praise came when tangible steps and timetables were given.

rubrics_metrics.name: fair_compensation_and_customer_remediation
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide clear, appropriate compensation and remedies to affected customers; be transparent about terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: United elected to provide passengers compensation equal to ticket cost and issued $500 vouchers; reports noted some communications suggested releases from lawsuits—compensation should not be perceived as coercive.

rubrics_metrics.name: preserve_evidence_and_cooperate_with_investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Retain video, recordings, reports, and personnel files and cooperate promptly with investigations and legal requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dao's lawyers asked courts to order preservation of all video and reports; United and the city agreed to preserve evidence. Prompt cooperation with authorities and investigators is a standard expectation.

rubrics_metrics.name: avoid_victim_blaming_or_premature_characterizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not publicly label or blame the affected individual before facts are verified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial United statements calling Dao "disruptive and belligerent" were contradicted by passenger accounts and video and contributed to criticism. Avoid assigning blame publicly until verified.

rubrics_metrics.name: limit_use_of_law_enforcement_for_customer_service_issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid involving police/security to remove paying, seated passengers except in true emergencies; revise policy accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Munoz announced United would no longer use police in involuntary bumping situations. PR and policy guidance after the incident emphasized not deploying law enforcement as a first resort in such scenarios.

rubrics_metrics.name: clarity_and_accuracy_about_facts_and_policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Be accurate and transparent about the factual situation and how company policies apply (e.g., overbooked vs. sold out, 'must-ride' status).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: United first described the flight as overbooked, later clarified it was sold out and employees were 'must-ride.' Inaccurate or shifting factual claims undermine trust and invite regulatory scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: review_and_reform_staff_training_and_standard_operating_procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Audit and update training and SOPs for frontline staff and contractors to prevent escalation and improper force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OIG found officers violated use-of-force policy; the incident prompted reviews and changes in training and labeling of airport security. Communications should reflect commitments to concrete training reforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: executive_accountability_and_leadership_actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Senior leaders should be held accountable in ways that are demonstrable and consistent with the severity of the incident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Munoz's planned promotion was delayed; critics called for resignation. PR recovery often requires visible leadership accountability (personnel review, governance actions, amended agreements tying compensation to customer experience improvements).

rubrics_metrics.name: frontline_staff_demeanor_and_diplomacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate and improve gate/onsite staff behavior: tone, diplomacy, and escalation practices matter in avoiding crises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passengers reported a terse, belligerent tone from a United supervisor which escalated the situation. Communications and training should emphasize de-escalation and customer diplomacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: operational_policies_to_prevent_last-minute_displacements
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement operational fixes (e.g., crew booking windows) to reduce need for involuntary removals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: United announced crews would be booked "at least 60 minutes prior to departure" to prevent last-minute seat reassignments—operational fixes support credibility of PR commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: regulatory_compliance_and_awareness_of_law_changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure public statements and policies comply with regulatory rules and be prepared for and responsive to regulatory changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USDOT later amended rules (effective April 2021) prohibiting removal after check-in; public communications should reflect current regulatory obligations and any changes in law prompted by incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: follow_up_reporting_and_transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Commit to and publish follow-up reports of reviews and reforms, and update the public on progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: United promised a detailed review and a report by a target date; follow-through and public reporting on progress (and failures) are critical to restoring trust.
